samples.summary: The `evicted` marker that makes a deleted-out-from-under-a-client append fail loudly is tab-local, so a purge/sweep performed in one tab leaves another tab's durable client silently appending into nothing while its chip still reports "Saved to this device".
samples.evidence: `evictedKeys` is a module-level `Map<dbName, Set<key>>` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts ~line 300, `const evictedKeys = new Map<string, Set<string>>()`), i.e. per JS realm. `purgeDocument` (line 937), `collectStale` (line 1226) and `dropAllForUser` (line 1147) all rely on `this.evicted.add(docKey)` so that a later `appendChange` hits `refuseIfEvicted` and the SDK repairs by writing a fresh snapshot. A second tab holding the same document has its own empty set: its `appendChange` finds no header, returns the contract's silent "no base" success (appendChange line 691-694), the SDK is never told, and `durable` is never lowered — so the chip keeps promising local durability for edits that are stored nowhere. The authors solved exactly this cross-realm problem for the logout erase by mirroring into `localStorage` (`DENIED_KEY` in offline-erase.ts:145, whose doc-comment describes this same failure), but the same reach was not given to eviction/purge/collection. Reachable on the ordinary path: delete a document (or run the once-per-session reconcile) in one tab while it is open in another.

samples.summary: The revocation reconcile deletes local entries on an *absence* from a listing, with no guard sparing entries whose change log holds un-pushed work — unlike eviction, which explicitly refuses to spend such an entry.
samples.evidence: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:487-497) keeps only ids present in `accessible` and calls `store.purgeDocument(id, {archives:'drop', skipOpen:true, updatedSince:listedAt})`. `purgeDocument` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:923-939) checks only liveness and timestamp; it never consults `changeCount`. By contrast `evictOldest` (line 1468) skips any entry with `changeCount > 0` precisely because "a non-empty log counts as unsent [work]" and deleting it destroys the only durable copy. So any listing that is merely incomplete — a read-replica lag, a future `take`/pagination added to `GET /documents` (the backend currently passes no `take`, document.controller.ts:190), a transient partial response — permanently deletes un-pushed edits for a document the user still has access to. `listedAt`/`isOpenElsewhere` do not cover it: an idle document last touched before the listing is the common case.

samples.summary: `DurableYorkieProvider` creates a `WafflebaseDocStore` per mounted durable document and never closes it, leaking an IndexedDB connection for every document opened in the session.
samples.evidence: The store is built in `useMemo(..., [userId])` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:148-189) and handed to the provider, but there is no `useEffect` cleanup calling `store.close()` anywhere in the component. Every other owner of a store closes it (`OfflineRuntime` cleanup, `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`, `purgeOfflineDocuments`, `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` all use `store.close()`), and `close()` exists specifically "so a `deleteDatabase` elsewhere is not blocked" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:~470). Two related leaks: `watchForOfflineDisable`'s fallback `new WafflebaseDocStore({userId: who})` (offline-erase.ts:546) is never closed, and `OfflineRuntime`'s cleanup `store.close()` (offline-runtime.tsx:208) runs while `collectStale`/`purge` may still be in flight — those calls transparently re-`open()` a fresh connection (open() memo is cleared by close()) that nothing ever closes.

samples.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments` puts its `try/catch` outside the loop, so a failure purging the first id silently abandons every remaining id.
samples.evidence: offline-erase.ts:402-412: `try { for (const id of documentIds) { await store.purgeDocument(...) } } catch (err) { console.warn(...) }`. A single transient IndexedDB failure (the state this module explicitly anticipates elsewhere — "a database that will not open under storage pressure is exactly the state a full disk produces") aborts the whole batch, so the local copies of documents 2..n survive a deletion the server has already accepted, with nothing scheduled to retry. The per-id loop should catch per iteration; compare `retryPendingOfflineErase`, which deliberately keeps going per user.

samples.summary: The lapse fallback reports `"another-tab"` for every non-durable reason it did not enumerate, so the tooltip asserts a document is being saved by another tab when the real reason is "no identity", "PDF document" or "the SDK refused the attach".
samples.evidence: collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299 — the chain tests `!supportsClientKey()`, `!permitted`, `!offlineEnabled` and then falls through unconditionally to `"another-tab"`. But `decided?.durable` is also false when `person` is undefined (line 351 guards on `!person`), when `docKey` starts with `pdf-` (`isExcluded`, use-durable-document.ts:41), and when `stoodDown === subject` (line 284). `LAPSE_REASONS['another-tab']` renders "This document is open in another tab, and that tab is the one saving it to this device" (sync-status-tooltip.ts:36-38) — a statement of fact that is false in those cases, on the one surface the design requires to "name which case applies".

samples.summary: `deleteFolder` cascades to the documents it contains on the server but never calls `purgeOfflineDocuments`, so those documents' local copies (and their content) survive the deletion until the next session's reconcile.
samples.evidence: Every other access-ending call site got the new purge: `deleteDocument` (documents.ts:167), `deleteDocuments` (documents.ts:215), `deleteWorkspace` (workspaces.ts:136), `removeMember` (workspaces.ts:167). `deleteFolder` (folders.ts:81-90) issues `DELETE /folders/:id` and does nothing local. If the backend deletes the documents inside the folder (the usual semantics), this is the same "content outlives the authority to read it" case the other four were changed for. Bounded by `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` on the next session, so the reach is limited — but the immediate guarantee the other call sites now make does not hold here.

samples.summary: `retryPendingOfflineErase()` runs under the identity that has just signed back in, so a previously-failed erase for *that same account* wipes the entries and archives this new session is concurrently writing, and rotates the device secret mid-session.
samples.evidence: offline-runtime.tsx:66 calls `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` (which re-permits writes via `permitOfflineWrites`, offline-erase.ts:81) and line 111 then awaits `retryPendingOfflineErase()`, which loops over every owed id — including `userId` itself when that account's own logout erase failed — and calls `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` → `dropAllForUser` + `forgetDeviceSecret(who)` (offline-erase.ts:32-39). `OfflineRuntime` is a sibling of `<Outlet/>` (PrivateRoute.tsx), so an editor can mount and begin persisting while that async retry is still running: its live entries are deleted, any archive of unrecoverable work for this user is dropped before `offerRecoverableWork` ever lists it, and `forgetDeviceSecret` changes `durableClientKey` for documents opened later in the same session, orphaning what the already-open ones are still writing under the old key.

samples.summary: On the involuntary-expiry path the remembered offline identity is never cleared, so `wafflebase-offline-user` outlives the session it names.
samples.evidence: auth.ts:134 — `if (eraseLocalData !== "none" && res?.ok) { await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout(); }`. `rememberOfflineUser(undefined)` is only reached from inside `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` (offline-erase.ts:313/337), so the 401 arm (`eraseLocalData: "none"`, auth.ts:~257) leaves the id in `localStorage` even though the session is over. `offlineUserId()` then keeps answering for a signed-out account, which is what `isOfflineUser` and both purge helpers key off. Harmless today because nothing runs while signed out, but it is an invariant ("the mirror is cleared the moment it is spent", offline-erase.ts:60) that this path breaks.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `evictedKeys` is a module-level Map keyed by dbName (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:206-215) and is reached per instance via the `evicted` getter (360-362), so the marker is per JS realm — the file's own comment at 201-204 concedes "Still tab-local". `appendChange` only throws when the mark is in THIS realm (691-694 -> refuseIfEvicted 749-758); otherwise it returns the contract's silent no-base success, and since durability is lowered only via a thrown failure reaching onWriteFailure (159-167, wired at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:161), the chip keeps reporting saved-locally. An unguarded reachable path exists: purgeOfflineDocuments (offline-erase.ts:393-413) calls purgeDocument with neither skipOpen nor updatedSince, so purgeDocument's isLive/isOpenElsewhere check at line 924 is skipped entirely on the server-accepted-delete path, while another tab holding the document keeps appending into nothing. The reconcile path (offline-erase.ts:492-496, skipOpen:true) and collectStale (isLiveAnywhere, 1212) are partially guarded, but collectStale's own comment (1218-1226) calls that guard "a best answer, not a proof", and neither guard covers the delete path. The file's mitigation argument ("loses the loud refusal, not the data") depends on SDK repair behavior I could not verify — @yorkie-js/sdk is declared in package.json:99 but not present in the tree — so no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) can be established. The authors solved the identical cross-realm problem for logout via a localStorage mirror (offline-erase.ts:127-145), which corroborates rather than refutes the concern.

finding.evidence: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:487-497) keeps only ids present in `accessible` and calls `store.purgeDocument(id, {archives:'drop', skipOpen:true, updatedSince:listedAt})`. `purgeDocument` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:923-939) checks only liveness and timestamp; it never consults `changeCount`. By contrast `evictOldest` (line 1468) skips any entry with `changeCount > 0` precisely because "a non-empty log counts as unsent [work]" and deleting it destroys the only durable copy. So any listing that is merely incomplete — a read-replica lag, a future `take`/pagination added to `GET /documents` (the backend currently passes no `take`, document.controller.ts:190), a transient partial response — permanently deletes un-pushed edits for a document the user still has access to. `listedAt`/`isOpenElsewhere` do not cover it: an idle document last touched before the listing is the common case.

verdict.reason: The quoted code facts are accurate (purgeDocument ignores changeCount; evictOldest checks it), but the loss path the finding depends on is guarded and the remaining behavior is deliberate. (1) The "merely incomplete listing" premise is unreachable: fetchDocuments (api/documents.ts:35-41) calls assertOk, which throws on any non-ok response (api/http-error.ts:1-10), and the caller awaits the listing before the purge and lets a failure throw, skipping both purge and recovery (offline-runtime.tsx:154-164). The backend GET /documents passes no skip/take/cursor and no trash filter (document.controller.ts:180-195), so no partial/paginated listing is produced, and no read-replica routing exists in packages/backend/src. (2) On the case the function actually fires on — genuine revocation — dropping un-pushed work is the explicit documented policy, not a missing guard: purgeDocument's contract (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:891-895) and docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:286-312 state that lost *access* drops the entry and its archives (the archive being the unsent-work copy) because recovery re-materializes readable content the user may no longer hold, and that the partial-listing safeguard is the caller's await/throw rather than a content-based exemption. evictOldest's changeCount check covers quota eviction, where access is intact and the work is still pushable — an asymmetry the design states deliberately. The requested guard would reinstate the invariant violation the reconcile exists to prevent.

finding.summary: Swallowing a failed `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently turns the loss path from "archive the work" into "delete the work" — the comment's claim that this "costs the chip its certainty, never the document" is wrong
finding.evidence: The new `watch()` helper catches a throwing `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...)` and only `console.warn`s. But that handler is the *only* caller of `durable.store.expectLoss(doc.getKey())`, and `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771, 791: `const losing = this.expectedLosses.has(documentKey)` / `if (record && losing)`) archives **only** when the latch is set; otherwise it deletes the snapshot, header and change log outright (lines 809-811). The SDK calls `remove()` on the three paths where local work could not be reconciled, so if the pinned SDK (`@yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.22`, per packages/frontend/package.json:99) rejects that event name — the exact scenario the new try/catch was added for — unsent edits are destroyed instead of archived, nothing is ever offered back by `offerRecoverableWork`, and because `reportLoss()` also never fires, `durable` stays true so the chip keeps reading "Saved to this device". That is simultaneously data loss and the over-report the feature says it must never make, with no signal beyond a console warning. If the event is genuinely unsupported the safe behaviour is to degrade the durability claim (e.g. latch `writesFailing`/`persistDisabled`) rather than proceed as if durability held.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the failed `local-changes-dropped` subscription is only `console.warn`ed, leaving `expectLoss` unlatched (so `remove()` deletes rather than archives) and `durable` still true. The code does neither. At durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:314-332 the `!watchingLoss` branch (a) calls `durable.store.expectLoss?.(doc.getKey())` inside its own try/catch, which is exactly the latch `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` reads at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:809/829 to take the archiving branch, and (b) calls `durable.reportUnreportable()`, which feeds the `!unreportable` conjunct of `durable` at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:194 and yields the `'unreportable'` lapse at :224 — so the chip stops claiming "Saved to this device". The same withdrawal is applied to the `persist-disabled` failure at :344-349. The finding's recommended remedy is already the implemented behavior; grep shows :309 is the only non-test subscription to that event, so no other copy of the described code exists.
